messages.content: writing a repeal and not a replace to leave it up to “more experienced authors” makes me question why yall would repeal in the first place. why not leave that up to more experienced authors?
esp given the resolution argues against the need for the resolution in the first place
seems like playing both sides to make the repeal appealing to more people
of course youre happy to “let the World Assembly judge” when your coauthors include the most powerful gcr delegate in the game and the mofa of another very influential region
and your reading of 23 makes sense but seems broad
and wa is about being specific

I’ll let you take a guess what’s more difficult, trawling through existing World Assembly resolutions to find what topics they do not cover and writing comprehensive legislation to cover all angles, or taking a look at a resolution that has not done this and finding it flawed. This seems borderline like a non-question.

I don’t know what this is meant to prove? Simone was neither Delegate nor an expected candidate at the time we brought him on board, so if it is a gotcha I can’t decipher for what, though you’re correct, I do in fact think concensus building by bringing authors of competing repeal drafts on the same topic on board is a pretty valid way of approaching the World Assembly.

TNP was always gonna rubberstamp anything of Simone’s even before he became Delegate. My point is that of course you’re gonna deflect criticism by saying “we’ll let the WA decide” when most of the vote is either directly controlled or directly influenced by the authors and regions friendly to them

“Letting the WA decide” doesn’t mean they favor quality resolutions. Libinjuncts tend to be pretty basic and boring and pass like nothing, while a wellresearched wellwritten TEP GP C/C is always gonna fail
It’s just a bad catch all for deflecting criticism
So in other words, a GA badge without GA-level hard work

I really don’t think anyone should pursue a repeal of a resolution that does a good thing without writing a better replacement. Of course it’s easy to find flaws with things and difficult to make things less flawed. But if you don’t even want to commit to trying the latter, I don’t think you should be doing the former

Any repeal without a replace should make an argument for why the regulation is not necessary; and this proposal doesn’t convince me that we shouldn’t ban forced blood sports, nor do I think it’s trying to, if I’m to take your responses at face value

It was a short line in response to a pretty subjective opinion, and you are deflecting as dishonestly as you accuse me of being if you pretend it was in any way a deflection of any substantial points by hyperfocussing on it.
repeal should be followed by replace in just abt every scenario as far as i'm concerned. i also agree with what a lot of aiv is saying hence my personal vote.
I'm not hyperfocusing on it. it appears that way because i mentioned it as one of four arguments against the repeal and it was one of two you replied to.
i see no more than those four arguments as worth having; it's not hyperfocusing to list it among all the things i find wrong with this

To be fair, I wasn't entirely sure what your argument with GA#23 was - a broad reading it might be, but it's also, I would argue, a pretty fundamental resolution the World Assembly - I don't think a broad reading is therefore unjustified.
And I'll be honest, I'm assuming the fourth is the argument whether a resolution on the topic is necessary in general?

Ah well let me rephrase that argument with more detail: In my opinion, the World Assembly is not meant to ever be as efficient as possible by relegating as many regulations as possible to as few resolutions as possible. Maybe forced blood sports fall under the penumbra of 23 if you think about it hard enough, but I think the WA should be as clear as possible with specific resolutions on specific areas, and I think that leaves a place for this resolution.

My other point was just that it seems the resolution is simultaneously arguing a resolution is not necessary (covered by GA23 or potentially by local law) while it (or at least the authors) remain ambivalent on replacements – it feels like trying to appeal to as many as possible rather than making a consistent argument

Thank you for clarifying - I'll attempt to address both points separately, even if we may still not see eye to eye here. Firstly: I think that's not an inherently invalid position, even if I personally am opposed to a greater number of GA resolutions, but I think it also takes away the necessity of those resolutions that means they are worthy of greater scrutiny - since they are not explicitly necessary and largely covered by previous legislation, one can hold them to a high standard when it comes to legislative practice, loopholes, etc. When a resolution is more fundamental to the WA, such flaws can more readily be excused for the greater good, but if the resolution is largely or even entirely redundant I think those should be strong considerations.

As for this one, I'm not sure why this is a huge consideration? I'm not convinced colouring the repeal with the views of one of three authors leads to a "consistent argument" - at that point you're attaching more weight to the author than to the resolution, I think, which to me feels like the wrong way of going about things.

well then imo dont have three authors of differing viewpoints. the consistency of the proposal, to me, is above the need for collaboration — if there is collaboration, then compromise shouldn’t be hard. to me, it strikes me as a repeal that’s unsure why we need to repeal the resolution. and if the repeal is unsure, then i’m definitely not convinced
Here's two campaign proposals for and against the resolution at vote
TEP votes against. Resolution passes. (6-3-0-0, including my former tiebreak)
